key_insight: Utonia shows that a single self-supervised point-transformer encoder can learn consistent, transferable representations across widely different point-cloud domains (remote sensing, LiDAR, RGB-D, CAD, and video-lifted clouds).
problem_solved: Eliminates the fragmentation caused by domain-specific 3D encoders by enabling one unified model to generalize across varying sensing geometries, densities, and priors.
method: Design and train one shared point-transformer encoder with self-supervised objectives across a mixture of diverse point-cloud datasets.
Apply domain-balanced sampling, normalization and augmentation strategies so the encoder learns modality-agnostic features despite heterogeneous point distributions.
Use unified pretext tasks (e.g., contrastive and/or masked modeling) to align representations from different domains into a common embedding space.
impact: Provides a practical route to a single pre-trained 3D backbone that can be fine-tuned for many downstream tasks, reducing engineering burden and improving transferability across scarce or new point-cloud domains.
visual_elements: Collage of point-cloud examples (remote sensing, outdoor LiDAR, indoor RGB-D, CAD, video-lifted) to show dataset diversity
Simplified block diagram of the shared point-transformer encoder and self-supervised training loop
2D embedding plot (t-SNE/UMAP) illustrating domain-mixed clusters indicating unified representations
Before/after or transfer bar chart showing improved downstream performance or reduced need for domain-specific models
paper_title: Utonia: Toward One Encoder for All Point Clouds
paper_authors: Yujia Zhang, Xiaoyang Wu, Yunhan Yang, Xianzhe Fan, Han Li
